symptom: A low-priority Deckle build still drove one CPU core and the fans to full speed; Task Manager showed every MSBuild node at BelowNormal and VBCSCompiler alone at Normal.
cause: Roslyn starts its compiler server through CreateProcess with an explicit NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS flag (BuildServerConnection.cs), which cancels the priority class a child would otherwise inherit from its BelowNormal MSBuild node. Measured on a Release build on 2026-11-06: 67 s of CPU in VBCSCompiler against 61 s in the four nodes together, so about half of the build ran at normal priority.
violatedInvariant: Every process a Deckle command-line build runs, the Roslyn compiler server included, runs at BelowNormal or lower.

must: Lower any running VBCSCompiler to BelowNormal from scripts/build-server-watchdog.ps1 at every tick, so a server started during a build is caught within one tick (Set-BuildServerLowPriority).
Leave a server already at BelowNormal or lower untouched: an operator who parked it at Idle keeps it.
mustNot: Disable shared compilation to get the low priority for free: an in-process compiler inherits BelowNormal, but a full rebuild takes twice as long (see dotnet-max-node-response-precedence).

automation.residual: The test exercises the lowering rule on a stand-in process. That a real build's server is reached within one tick was observed by hand on 2026-11-06 (BelowNormal three seconds after a forced recompile of Deckle.Core); the first seconds of a build, before the watchdog's first tick, still run at Normal.
